content: 1. Drospirenone may increase the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of ibrutinib through its impact on CYP3A4-mediated metabolism in the liver and intestines. The clinical relevance of this interaction remains uncertain. 3. Drospirenone has the potential to increase the levels or effects of idelalisib by altering CYP3A4 enzyme activity in hepatic and intestinal pathways. The significance of this interaction is not well established. 4. Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of ifosfamide by modulating the metabolism via the CYP3A4 enzyme system. The clinical implications of this interaction are unclear. 5. Drospirenone could increase the levels or effects of imatinib by affecting CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. The clinical importance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Ethinylestradiol may reduce the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of adverse effects associated with TCAs. 7. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of indinavir by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme activity in the liver and intestines. The clinical significance of this interaction is not determined. 8. Drospirenone may elevate the levels of iodinated glycerol by decreasing renal clearance, potentially leading to hyperkalemia. The clinical relevance of this interaction is uncertain. 9. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of irinotecan by modulating CYP3A4-mediated metabolism in hepatic and intestinal pathways. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 10. Drospirenone may enhance the levels or effects of isosorbide dinitrate by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme activity in the liver and intestines. The clinical implications of this interaction are unclear. 11. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of itraconazole by influencing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism in hepatic and intestinal pathways. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well established. 12. Drospirenone may elevate the levels of magnesium chloride, magnesium citrate, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium oxide, and magnesium sulfate by reducing renal clearance. The clinical relevance of these interactions is uncertain. 13. Maitake mushroom may enhance the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of maraviroc by modulating CYP3A4 enzyme activity in hepatic and intestinal pathways. The clinical implications of this interaction are unclear. 15. Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of methadone by influencing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism in the liver and intestines. The clinical significance of this interaction is not determined. 16. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by modulating CYP3A4 enzyme activity in hepatic and intestinal pathways. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Drospirenone may enhance the effects of minoxidil through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well established. 18. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of montelukast by influencing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism in hepatic and intestinal pathways. The clinical implications of this interaction are unclear. 19. Drospirenone may elevate the levels or effects of naloxegol by modulating CYP3A4 enzyme activity in hepatic and intestinal pathways. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of nifedipine by influencing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism in hepatic and intestinal pathways. The clinical relevance of this interaction is not determined.
